tagline: Up the Blanchard to where the song was written.
intro: From Ottawa the byway works upstream along the Blanchard River on US 224 and SR 37, past Gilboa and east to Findlay, then south with the river toward Mount Blanchard, through rural farm country. The river is named for Jean Jacques Blanchard, a French tailor who settled among the Shawnee along it in 1769, and one of its old names is Tailor's River.

In 1908 Tell Taylor wrote "Down by the Old Mill Stream" on its banks at Findlay. His friends, the story goes, told him it had no commercial value. Its sheet music has since sold more than four million copies.

moments.title: Ottawa's Third Street
moments.text: A mile of brick street, laid in the early 1900s, runs between Victorian houses and shade trees to Waterworks Park.

moments.title: Gilboa
moments.text: A 16-foot fiberglass bull stands along US 224 across from the grain elevator, and nearby a through Pratt truss bridge from the 1800s crosses the Blanchard.

moments.title: Great Karg Well
moments.text: The Karg gas well came in with a roar on January 20, 1886, and for more than four months its towering flame could not be contained, in a town booming on oil and gas.
